lane.name: Punk and hardcore roots
lane.definition: Ramones, Black Flag, Minor Threat: the punk foundation under cowpunk, SST and the DIY network.

albums.label: Sire
albums.description: Fourteen buzzsaw songs in under half an hour, stripped to bare chords, deadpan vocals and cartoon-tough-guy lyrics, laid down the American punk template. Its speed, brevity and DIY simplicity became a foundation the later hardcore and indie underground built on. The essential starting point for this whole lane.
albums.lineage: Its deadpan drone and deliberate amateurism sound indebted to the Velvet Underground and proto-indie scene (V29); this branch runs forward into hardcore, cowpunk and the college-rock underground rather than continuing V29's own art-rock line.

albums.label: Sire
albums.description: A quick, tighter-sounding second album that keeps the debut's speed and joke-laden lyrics while sharpening the production slightly, proving the formula wasn't a one-off. It cemented the band's rapid album-a-year work rate that fed the DIY ethic later scenes copied. A solid second landmark for hearing the sound consolidate.
albums.lineage: Continues the Ramones' minimalism, which sounds indebted to Velvet Underground deadpan (V29), toward the hardcore and DIY scenes that followed; not part of V29's own art-rock trajectory.

albums.label: Sire
albums.description: The band's most melodic early record layers surf and bubblegum-pop hooks onto the same buzzsaw formula, and several of its songs became punk standards. It shows the pop songcraft hiding inside the Ramones' minimalism that later power-pop and cowpunk bands drew on. A key third landmark rounding out the band's classic run.
albums.lineage: Extends the Ramones' minimalist sound, indebted to V29's deadpan simplicity, with stronger pop hooks, feeding forward into power pop and the DIY underground rather than back into V29's own catalog.

albums.label: CBS/Epic
albums.description: The Clash's genre-sprawling double album folds rockabilly, reggae, ska and R&B into a punk base, proving the genre could absorb roots music without losing its edge. Its rockabilly and roots-rock detours anticipate the genre-crossing instincts of the US cowpunk bands that followed. Included here as the UK punk landmark closest in spirit to cowpunk.
albums.lineage: Represents the UK punk scene running alongside this lane's American hardcore lineage; its rockabilly-and-reggae blending resembles what cowpunk and LA roots punk (V14) would do next.

albums.label: Frontier Records
albums.description: Fourteen songs blaze past in about fifteen minutes on this LA hardcore debut, fronted by ex-Black Flag singer Keith Morris and stripped down to pure speed and sneering humor. Its extreme brevity and release on the independent Frontier label make it a textbook early hardcore record. A tight, essential companion to Damaged for the early-'80s LA hardcore scene.
albums.lineage: Grows directly out of the same Hermosa Beach/LA hardcore scene as Black Flag (a former member founded the band); feeds the American hardcore underground (V16) and DIY network rather than back into earlier NY punk.

albums.label: Cherry Red Records
albums.description: Jello Biafra's surf-guitar-inflected San Francisco hardcore debut pairs breakneck tempos with pointed political satire aimed at California politics and American complacency. East Bay Ray's twangy, reverb-soaked leads give it a sound unlike any other hardcore band of the moment. Essential for the political-satire wing of the punk foundation this lane covers.
albums.lineage: Runs parallel to Black Flag's Southern California hardcore; Biafra's own Alternative Tentacles label ties the band to the American hardcore underground (V16) and the broader DIY network rather than back toward V29.

albums.label: SST
albums.description: Henry Rollins' first full album with the band turns suburban California rage into lurching, brutal hardcore, released on Greg Ginn's own SST label. Ginn's jagged, atonal guitar and Rollins' bellowed vocals make it harsher and stranger than most punk of its day. Essential for understanding the SST label ethic that later shaped indie distribution.
albums.lineage: Takes the punk template of peers like the Ramones into a harder, more nihilistic hardcore sound; as the flagship band of Ginn's SST label it feeds directly into the SST/college-rock underground (V16) rather than back toward V29.

albums.label: ROIR
albums.description: A Washington, D.C. band of jazz-trained musicians plays hardcore at breakneck, technically dazzling speed and then drops into reggae interludes, originally released only on cassette by ROIR. Alongside Black Flag and Minor Threat it set the standard for early-80s American hardcore's intensity and musicianship. A key landmark showing the genre's virtuosic, genre-hopping edge.
albums.lineage: The band's DC shows helped ignite the local hardcore scene that produced Minor Threat; it feeds into the American hardcore underground (V16) and later crossover thrash rather than back toward V29's art-rock roots.

albums.label: SST
albums.description: The infamous side two slows hardcore tempos to a doom-metal crawl, alienating the band's original audience but pointing directly at the slow, heavy sound that would become sludge and slowcore's noisier cousins. It shows SST hardcore mutating away from its own founding formula within a few years. A useful landmark for how quickly the scene's rules got broken from the inside.
albums.lineage: Splits from Black Flag's own faster hardcore template (this lane) into slow, sludgy tempos that anticipate noise rock and slowcore textures; feeds forward into SST's own stranger later catalog and indirectly into post-punk/noise rock (X10) rather than back to the Core.

albums.label: Dischord Records
albums.description: This Dischord compilation gathers the band's early-'80s EPs and stray tracks, and is the canonical way to hear Ian MacKaye's foundational straight-edge hardcore. Tight, fast and moralistic, it set both a musical and an ethical template (DIY labels, no drugs, no sellouts) that the American hardcore underground inherited. Essential for the DIY-network trunk line this lane sits under.
albums.lineage: Came out of the DC hardcore scene that Bad Brains had ignited; through MacKaye's own Dischord label it feeds directly into the DIY-label model and the American underground/college rock scene (V16) rather than back toward earlier UK or NY punk.
